mission.title: Thataway
mission.description: Track down Halborn and bring him to a meeting with the Merovingian.

npc.say: I said I'll be there. Move it along!

Huh. I could. They'll probably try to--
What? Northwest. Look, mind your own business. I've got to handle this myself. He'd see you clowns coming a mile off, anyway.
No-o problems. We're just like peas in a pod here.
He's got a bit of an inferiority complex, if you ask me.
That is a conversation for another time, yes? We would not want to...distract our guest.

phase.briefing:
Funny thing about that Halborn: he's *still* determined to get the program he's been after, even though everyone's told him that it isn't even in the Matrix--not to mention that he just killed the woman who wrote it.
He may be clueless, but he hasn't let that stop him yet. He's begun ratcheting things up by attacking Carlyne directly; might have got somewhere with it, too, except that operatives bailed Carlyne out.
Poor Halborn. Finding himself in these rather desperate straits, Halborn might be a little more forthcoming with details about the program. The trick is finding him; he hasn't exactly stayed in touch. Override programs are still appearing here and there, though, so we'll start with those, hm?

enter.say: I've got override activity in there, as well as redpill readings. They aren't ours.

near.say: Zionites--lovely. And no Halborn. Hm... We'd better finish them off. They may have snatched useful.

objective.text: Take the access card from the Zionite

done.say: An access card? Let me check this thing out... Uh-huh... Okay, I think we've got a match for the place that uses the code on that thing. Maybe we can pick up some juicy info.

phase.briefing:
If you keep coming up with results, I may have to find someone else to give all the fluff missions to...
But I'm getting ahead of myself. You still have plenty of time to screw this up.

enter.say: The Merv's records say the access card is registered to an apartment there. I'm reading some computer activity, so maybe they have a system we can tap into for information.

done.say:
Ooh. Now that's what I'm talking about. Hiding their removable media in the dresser--oh, they're clever.
Upload that to me, and I'll rifle through it.

objective.text: Upload the removable media at a hardline

phase.briefing:
Ugh, what is this mess you've uploaded, {player}? Oh, the foul bits of data I have to sort through when dealing with operatives...
Hm... Intelligence reports... They *have* been trying to locate Halborn... Let me see...
Ah. Their intelligence was limited--naturally--but correlating it with our own information produced some interesting results. Try there.

enter.say: Picking up overrides in the area... Could be money.

talk.say:
Damn it, I've got Oracle-lovers and that skinny prat all over me, and you want to chat?
So, maybe you did help me out before. ...
All right, but you make damn sure you keep them off my back in the mean time, got it?

done.say: I didn't actually think it was possible for him to get any more rude than he was before...but he's proven me wrong!

phase.briefing: I don't think Halborn properly understands his situation. He only succeeded in finding the Oracle because we got him away from Carlyne. Terminating the Oracle was useful to us, but if he expects further assistance, he'll have to give as well as receive, mm? Quid pro quo.

enter.say: The meeting's going down. Halborn better mind his P's and Q's around the boss.

talk.say:
You're nuts if you think I can give out any more information about it with Carlyne around trying to use anything he can find against me. I'm going to have to take him down... It's the only way, now. And I think I know how to do it. I just have to find his damn ship.
He isn't so smart. Only reason he got the jump on me in the first place was because he was just 800 miles away from here...

Interesting...
As you say, monsieur. We will leave him in your capable hands. The man who killed the Oracle can easily deal with a pest like him. And of course, if you do need to locate his...eh...ship, it would be a simple matter for you to get the information from the Machines.

mission.finish:
Bah. I don't know why we even bother trying to talk with the man. He's obviously determined to go it alone, so why should we lift a finger?
And frankly, I wouldn't put much faith in his so-called facts and figures. He's about as reliable as the internet when it comes to factual data.
